text: Time-resolved, context-aware bacterial phylogenetics for public health
textPreview: Time-resolved, context-aware bacterial phylogenetics for public health

text:
Open with the operational question: once we know several isolates share an ST, can we tell whether that lineage has been circulating locally or has been introduced repeatedly? This talk is about the evidence needed to ask that question safely. Aim for about 45 seconds.

[Sources]
- https://github.com/ghruproject/chronoclade

title: The public-health question starts where MLST stops

name: slide-2-title
text: The public-health question starts where MLST stops
textPreview: The public-health question starts where MLST stops

text: One local group is sampled repeatedly through time.
textPreview: One local group is sampled repeatedly through time.

text: Local isolates sit in separated groups beside different contextual genomes.
textPreview: Local isolates sit in separated groups beside different contextual genomes.

text:
MLST is a useful first stratification, but the same ST can contain very different public-health histories. The left-hand pattern is consistent with local persistence. The right-hand pattern is consistent with repeated introductions. Whole-genome topology, distances, dates and public context are needed to distinguish them. About 75 seconds.

[Sources]
- https://github.com/ghruproject/chronoclade

title: Sampling dates can translate genetic change into calendar time

name: slide-3-title
text: Sampling dates can translate genetic change into calendar time
textPreview: Sampling dates can translate genetic change into calendar time

text: A dated tree estimates rates and the timing of ancestral nodes.
textPreview: A dated tree estimates rates and the timing of ancestral nodes.

text:
• Mutations accumulate along branches.
• Tips sampled at different times provide calibration points.
• A clock model estimates substitutions per site per year.
• The branch lengths can then be expressed in dates.
textPreview: • Mutations accumulate along branches. | • Tips sampled at different times provide calibration points. | • A clock model estimates substi...

text: Only if the lineage evolved measurably over the sampling window.
textPreview: Only if the lineage evolved measurably over the sampling window.

text:
The tree initially measures change in substitutions per site, not years. Sampling dates at the tips can calibrate a molecular clock. TreeTime uses an approximate maximum-likelihood framework to estimate rates and node dates efficiently. The crucial qualification is that the dates must contain measurable information about evolutionary change. About 90 seconds.

[Sources]
- https://academic.oup.com/ve/article/4/1/vex042/4794731
- https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1483140/

title: The minimum input is small—but its quality matters

name: slide-4-title
text: The minimum input is small—but its quality matters
textPreview: The minimum input is small—but its quality matters

text: Assemblies or a core-genome alignment from sufficiently close isolates.
textPreview: Assemblies or a core-genome alignment from sufficiently close isolates.

text: At least year and month where possible; uncertainty must be retained.
textPreview: At least year and month where possible; uncertainty must be retained.

text: Analyse species separately and normally work within an ST or narrower clonal group.
textPreview: Analyse species separately and normally work within an ST or narrower clonal group.

text: Focal versus contextual origin, location and coded patient or facility fields where available.
textPreview: Focal versus contextual origin, location and coded patient or facility fields where available.

text:
The basic data contract is one row per genome. We need a stable isolate identifier, the assembly path, a collection date, species, lineage or ST, and whether the sample is focal or context. Patient identifiers can be coded and are optional. Dates can be year-only, but month-level data improve resolution. Emphasise that this is a modest metadata requirement. About 75 seconds.

[Sources]
- https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1483140/
- https://github.com/ghruproject/chronoclade

title: Bacterial genomes make the clock harder to read

name: slide-5-title
text: Bacterial genomes make the clock harder to read
textPreview: Bacterial genomes make the clock harder to read

text: Imported DNA can add many changes at once and distort both distances and branch lengths.
textPreview: Imported DNA can add many changes at once and distort both distances and branch lengths.

text: Slow evolution, narrow sampling windows or clustered dates may leave too few substitutions to calibrate time.
textPreview: Slow evolution, narrow sampling windows or clustered dates may leave too few substitutions to calibrate time.

text: Sparse or geographically uneven public sampling can make an introduction look like local persistence—or vice versa.
textPreview: Sparse or geographically uneven public sampling can make an introduction look like local persistence—or vice versa.

text: Correct recombination · test the dates · show the contextual sampling
textPreview: Correct recombination · test the dates · show the contextual sampling

text:
This is why a bacterial time tree is not simply a tree plus dates. Homologous recombination violates a simple clonal tree model, so ChronoClade uses ClonalFrameML before calculating clonal distances or temporal signal. Bacterial evolution may also be too slow over two years, and public context will always be incomplete. About 90 seconds.

[Sources]
- https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004041
- https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1483140/
- https://github.com/ghruproject/chronoclade

title: Published datasets show why root-to-tip is only a diagnostic

name: slide-6-title
text: Published datasets show why root-to-tip is only a diagnostic
textPreview: Published datasets show why root-to-tip is only a diagnostic

text: The regression placed the MRCA near day 0, supporting diversification during the infection.
textPreview: The regression placed the MRCA near day 0, supporting diversification during the infection.

text: A modest fit was still informative—and the independent date-randomisation test passed.
textPreview: A modest fit was still informative—and the independent date-randomisation test passed.

text: It looked clock-like, but the dates were not more informative than chance.
textPreview: It looked clock-like, but the dates were not more informative than chance.

text: Roe et al. · Frontiers in Microbiology 2019
textPreview: Roe et al. · Frontiers in Microbiology 2019

text: Reliable estimates generally needed sampling windows of about 15 years or more.
textPreview: Reliable estimates generally needed sampling windows of about 15 years or more.

text: Explore with root-to-tip; make the decision with a randomisation test.
textPreview: Explore with root-to-tip; make the decision with a randomisation test.

text:
These are published bacterial datasets, not simulated points. Pseudomonas within one patient produced a clear association and an MRCA near admission. Typhi had only an R-squared of 0.12 but a highly significant slope and passed the randomisation test. Klebsiella ST101 is the warning case: a positive slope, but 10,000 permutations gave P equals 0.339. The large tuberculosis study found very weak fits and showed that slow organisms often need much longer sampling windows. The lesson is that R-squared is descriptive, not the gate. About two minutes.

[Sources]
- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22814-9
- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-018-07370-z
- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2019.00542/full
- https://journals.plos.org/plospathogens/article?id=10.1371/journal.ppat.1008067

title: Published date-randomisation tests change the decision

name: slide-7-title
text: Published date-randomisation tests change the decision
textPreview: Published date-randomisation tests change the decision

text: Observed clock-rate estimates did not overlap the randomisations.
textPreview: Observed clock-rate estimates did not overlap the randomisations.

text: 145 genomes selected from a global set of 300
textPreview: 145 genomes selected from a global set of 300

text: 10,000 permutations gave P = 0.339: do not treat the clock as established.
textPreview: 10,000 permutations gave P = 0.339: do not treat the clock as established.

text: Roe et al. · Frontiers in Microbiology 2019
textPreview: Roe et al. · Frontiers in Microbiology 2019

text: A defensible workflow must be allowed to say: do not produce a time tree.
textPreview: A defensible workflow must be allowed to say: do not produce a time tree.

text:
Here are four real applications of date randomisation. Mycobacterium leprae has an unusually strong signal because ancient genomes extend the calibration window. Typhi 3.1.1 and Klebsiella ST17 both passed, supporting dated analyses. Klebsiella ST101 did not: despite a positive slope, 10,000 permutations gave a non-significant result. That is precisely why the pipeline must permit an indeterminate output and suppress the dated tree when the evidence gate fails. About two minutes.

[Sources]

title: From dated genomes to a time tree: four conceptual steps

name: slide-8-title
text: From dated genomes to a time tree: four conceptual steps
textPreview: From dated genomes to a time tree: four conceptual steps

text: Align related genomes and correct recombination.
textPreview: Align related genomes and correct recombination.

text: Use the most precise dates available; retain uncertainty.
textPreview: Use the most precise dates available; retain uncertainty.

text: Only when the dates carry more information than chance.
textPreview: Only when the dates carry more information than chance.

text: The software can vary; the scientific logic does not.
textPreview: The software can vary; the scientific logic does not.

text:
Keep the workflow conceptual. First reconstruct the clonal evolutionary history, correcting recombination. Second attach collection dates with their real precision. Third ask whether those dates explain more divergence than random dates. Only then fit the molecular clock and express branches in calendar time. TreeTime, BactDating or other software can implement parts of this logic; the key point is the evidence gate. About 90 seconds.

[Sources]
- https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004041
- https://academic.oup.com/ve/article/4/1/vex042/4794731
- https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/46/22/e134/5078231
- https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1483140/

title: A time-scaled tree places evolution on a calendar

name: slide-9-title
text: A time-scaled tree places evolution on a calendar
textPreview: A time-scaled tree places evolution on a calendar

text:
• Tips are anchored by collection date
• Horizontal position represents calendar time
• Internal nodes are estimated ancestral dates
• Uncertainty belongs with every date estimate
textPreview: • Tips are anchored by collection date | • Horizontal position represents calendar time | • Internal nodes are estimated ancestral dates ...

text: It estimates when ancestors existed—not who infected whom.
textPreview: It estimates when ancestors existed—not who infected whom.

text:
A time-scaled tree has the same topology as an evolutionary tree, but its horizontal axis is calendar time. The observed tips are anchored by collection dates. The clock model estimates when internal ancestors existed and attaches uncertainty to those dates. It does not reconstruct a chain of person-to-person transmission. About 90 seconds.

[Sources]
- https://academic.oup.com/ve/article/4/1/vex042/4794731
- https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1483140/

title: Adding time lets us ask better public-health questions

name: slide-10-title
text: Adding time lets us ask better public-health questions
textPreview: Adding time lets us ask better public-health questions

text: When did this lineage begin circulating locally?
textPreview: When did this lineage begin circulating locally?

text: Do isolates sampled two years apart share a recent ancestor?
textPreview: Do isolates sampled two years apart share a recent ancestor?

text: Are later cases nested within earlier local diversity?
textPreview: Are later cases nested within earlier local diversity?

text: Does the pattern favour persistence, repeated introduction—or neither?
textPreview: Does the pattern favour persistence, repeated introduction—or neither?

text: Then interpret the tree alongside patient, place and sampling context.
textPreview: Then interpret the tree alongside patient, place and sampling context.

text:
Time does not answer these questions automatically, but it makes them testable. We can ask when a local group shared an ancestor, whether later isolates descend from diversity already seen locally, and whether the sampled pattern is more consistent with persistence or repeated introduction. Those remain hypotheses until combined with patient, place and contextual sampling. About 90 seconds.

[Sources]
- https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1483140/
- https://academic.oup.com/ve/article/4/1/vex042/4794731

title: Time-resolved phylogenetics sharpens decisions—but does not replace epidemiology

name: slide-11-title
text: Time-resolved phylogenetics sharpens decisions—but does not replace epidemiology
textPreview: Time-resolved phylogenetics sharpens decisions—but does not replace epidemiology

text:
• Places genetic divergence in calendar time
• Tests whether the sampling dates are genuinely informative
• Distinguishes persistence and repeated-introduction hypotheses
• Focuses the next epidemiological investigation
• Makes uncertainty and sampling limitations explicit
textPreview: • Places genetic divergence in calendar time | • Tests whether the sampling dates are genuinely informative | • Distinguishes persistence...

text:
• Direct transmission between people
• An exact number of introduction events
• A universal SNP threshold
• Complete global context from incomplete public sampling
• Reliable dates when temporal signal is absent
textPreview: • Direct transmission between people | • An exact number of introduction events | • A universal SNP threshold | • Complete global context...

text: Best used as a genomic evidence layer within public-health review.
textPreview: Best used as a genomic evidence layer within public-health review.

text:
The benefit is not simply a prettier tree. It is a more disciplined question and a transparent chain from data to interpretation. It can focus epidemiological review and highlight where more sampling is worth doing. But it is not a transmission tree, it cannot count introductions directly and it remains sensitive to incomplete context and missing metadata. About 90 seconds.

[Sources]
- https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1483140/
- https://github.com/ghruproject/chronoclade
An ordinary phylogeny shows shared ancestry, but not when those ancestors existed.
textPreview: An ordinary phylogeny shows shared ancestry, but not when those ancestors existed.

text: Dates only help when evolution is measurable
textPreview: Dates only help when evolution is measurable

text: A two-year sampling window may—or may not—contain enough genetic change.
textPreview: A two-year sampling window may—or may not—contain enough genetic change.

text: No temporal signal is a valid result; do not force a time tree.
textPreview: No temporal signal is a valid result; do not force a time tree.

text: Which E. coli or Klebsiella ST do we have genomes and year/month dates for?
textPreview: Which E. coli or Klebsiella ST do we have genomes and year/month dates for?

text:
Close on three ideas. Relatedness alone does not supply a calendar. Sampling dates only help when sufficient change accumulated over the observed window. Temporal signal must therefore be tested before dating, and a negative result is scientifically useful. Then invite discussion about which E. coli or Klebsiella ST has the minimum data needed to try this. About one minute.

[Sources]
- https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1483140/
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25771196/
